standard_text: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 multiplication worksheets: the standard algorithm for 3-digit by 2-digit, 4-digit by 2-digit and 3-digit by 3-digit numbers, placeholder zeros, zeros inside numbers, word problems and estimating to check. 100 practice questions with step-by-step answers.
key_big: Multiply by one digit at a time, one row per digit. Then add the rows.
key_sub: The tens row starts with one placeholder zero and the hundreds row with two: 346 × 27 = 2,422 + 6,920 = 9,342. Estimate first to check the answer.
body_html:
One row for each digit

The standard algorithm multiplies the top number by one digit of the bottom number at a time. Each digit gives one row, called a partial product. Then you add the rows.

3-digit × 2-digit

Row 1 multiplies by the ones digit. Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it starts with a placeholder zero (green) in the ones place.

3-digit × 3-digit

A 3-digit bottom number gives three rows. The hundreds row starts with two zeros.

Zero inside a number

405 × 32 = ?

Row 1: 5 × 2 = 10, write 0, regroup 1. 0 × 2 + 1 = 1. 4 × 2 = 8. So 405 × 2 = 810. Row 2: write 0, then 405 × 3 = 1,215, so 12,150. Add: 810 + 12,150 = 12,960.

Answer: 12,960

Estimate to check

Round each number to its greatest place and multiply in your head. 346 × 27 is about 300 × 30 = 9,000, so 9,342 makes sense. An answer like 3,114 or 93,420 is far off.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
No zero in row 2 (346 × 27 = 2,422 + 692)Row 2 is × 20, so write 0 first: 6,920
Only one zero in the hundreds row× 100s needs two zeros: 253 × 100 = 25,300
Forgetting a regrouped digit (346 × 7 = 2,182)Write it above the next column and add it
Adding the regrouped digit firstMultiply first, then add: 4 × 7 + 4 = 32
Skipping the 0 in 405 (405 × 2 = 90)0 × 2 = 0, then add the regrouped 1: 810

faq.q: How do you teach multi-digit multiplication in 5th grade?
faq.a: Use the standard algorithm: one row for each digit of the bottom number, a placeholder zero for the tens row and two for the hundreds row, then add the rows. Ask children to estimate first so they can check the answer.

faq.q: Why do you add a zero when multiplying by a 2-digit number?
faq.a: In 346 × 27 the 2 means 2 tens, so the second row is 346 × 20, not 346 × 2. The zero in the ones place makes the row 6,920 instead of 692.

faq.q: How do you multiply a 3-digit number by a 3-digit number?
faq.a: Write three rows: the number times the ones digit, times the tens digit (one zero first), and times the hundreds digit (two zeros first). Add the three rows, for example 253 × 146 = 1,518 + 10,120 + 25,300 = 36,938.
It is the Common Core Grade 5 standard for fluently multiplying multi-digit whole numbers with the standard algorithm, for example a 3- or 4-digit number by a 2-digit number.
